thesis: A five-colour Dragon deck that buys its own curve down and then taxes every Dragon that enters — one arrival multiplies into several, each arrival is priced in damage and cards — whose kill is PROVEN on a board and unproven as a board you can reach.

stages.label: THE FIVE-COLOUR TOLL
stages.what_it_does:
Pays for a nine-mana commander and a 22-Dragon top end out of 36 land copies (31 entries), six rocks and three land-fetching sorceries — Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim — which is this stage's 40 cards. It is still the binding stage, and V2 moved it further than a patch label suggests. Five spells became five lands and every figure here went with them: mean available mana 4.219 to 4.534 at turn five and 4.669 to 5.101 at six, the turn-five land drop 0.525 to 0.649, the commander never cast by turn ten 7,170 to 5,997 of 10,000, cast by turn six 4.1% to 5.8%.

15 of 36 lands enter tapped (42%, five of them always), still over the one-in-three budget mana_analysis flags. Colour is not even: green on-curve 0.831 from lands alone, white and blue 0.670, red 0.610, black 0.261 on 9 land sources — lowest of the five, with no Swamp in the 99. Rocks and dorks lift black to 0.563.

What four of the five arrivals cost is LIFE: Mana Confluence per activation, Shivan Reef per coloured mana (as damage), Prismatic Vista one plus itself, Sacred Foundry two to enter untapped — in a deck whose Moltensteel Dragon also buys power with life, and whose logged game 001 spent 16 for 12 under a Blood Moon lock. Cavern of Souls is the exception, and its rider is not mana at all: a Dragon spell paid with its mana can't be countered.

Mox Jasper stays blank until a Dragon is on the battlefield and Dragon's Hoard banks a counter per Dragon entering, so conversion feeds this stage back. A Treasure is a one-shot stockpile spent only when lands and rocks fall short: it does not raise average mana, it buys the one expensive turn a nine-drop needs.

stages.label: THE PRICE CUT
stages.what_it_does:
What has to happen before the deck is doing its thing is that a Dragon becomes affordable ahead of curve, and half of that is already true on turn one. Eminence works from the command zone: other Dragon spells cost {1} less with nothing to cast, nothing to resolve and nothing an opponent can remove. The other half is four printed reducers — Urza's Incubator {2}, Dragonspeaker Shaman {2}, Herald's Horn {1}, Dragonlord's Servant {1}. An oracle scan of all 95 entries for 'less to cast' returns exactly those four plus eminence; Cavern-Hoard Dragon's self-reduction left with V2.

Priced: a reducer drawn is 0.523 assembled, 0.419 by turn six, mean turn 3.298. At four cards it is 25.8% of opening sevens and 32.1% by turn three, against the cited yardstick that '5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%'. It is NOT the thinnest thing here: deck-audit flags thin at size 3 or less and three components carry the flag — Dragon-restricted mana at 2, THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg at 2, and THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg at 3. The fourteen sizes run 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 8, 9, 9, so this group is the smallest the audit does not flag. Reducer AND ramp together, the turn-five Ur-Dragon hand, is 0.424 / 0.292 at mean turn 4.486.

Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug are a separate two-card component (0.304 / 0.232) because their mana is spendable only on Dragon spells: manabase.land_colors scores restricted mana as zero sources, correct for colour maths and exactly wrong for 'can I cast a Dragon'. Desolation is also a one-sided sweeper — 3 damage to each non-Dragon creature.

The commander's body is not part of ignition in practice: mean cast turn 8.138, 5.8% by turn six, not cast by turn ten in 5,997 of 10,000 iterations — V1 read 8.172 / 4.1% / 7,170.

stages.label: TREASURE, TUTORS AND THE TOP OF THE LIBRARY
stages.what_it_does:
What keeps the engine running once a Dragon has landed: Treasure, a specific Dragon on demand, and cards.

Five of the declaration's six Treasure sources are here — Atsushi, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone, Rapacious Dragon and Smothering Tithe (the sixth, Smaug the Magnificent, is under wincon: its Treasure count is what its own attack trigger deals). V2 cut Cavern-Hoard Dragon, so the group is six and its drawn rate falls from 0.732 assembled / 0.618 by turn six / mean turn 2.897 to 0.673 / 0.558 / 3.053. Eight of the nine targets that kept their labels through V2 read HIGHER; this group and the two-card Dragon-restricted one (0.306 to 0.304) are the two that fell — the price of the land base. That figure is complete; every Treasure-derived MANA figure is a floor instead, because four of the six (Atsushi, Goldspan, Old Gnawbone, Smothering Tithe) are named in meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled and only Rapacious Dragon's ETB and Smaug's upkeep reach the mana model. Klauth's spells-only attack mana left with V2 too; deck-facts' restricted-mana note names Cavern of Souls in its place.

The three Dragonstorm enchantments each return to their owner's hand when a Dragon you control enters, which makes them recurring rather than one-shot: Encroaching fetches two basics, Roiling draws two and discards one, Breaching free-casts a nonland card of mana value 8 or less. That recursion is a genuine conversion-to-fuel loop and it is printed on no payoff — it is printed on the fuel.

Finding a Dragon is three cards wide: Sarkhan's Triumph, Worldly Tutor and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon (filed in mana). Korlessa, Scale Singer is the fourth route and the cheapest Dragon in the 99 at mana value 2 — she lets you cast Dragons off the top, compounding with the eminence discount.

stages.label: ONE ARRIVAL BECOMES SEVERAL
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper, and it has two families under one roof.

ENTRY. Miirym copies every other nontoken Dragon; Panharmonicon doubles every trigger an entering creature or artifact causes; Lathliss makes a 5/5 per nontoken Dragon; Ancient Gold Dragon rolls a d20 on combat damage; Utvara Hellkite makes a 6/6 per attacking Dragon; Sneak Attack puts one from hand for {R}; Hellkite Courser is the only card in the 99 that puts a commander onto the battlefield from the command zone, and 005 refutes Sneak Attack doing it.

SPOF STAYS NULL, and 007 is why that needs an argument rather than a value: without Panharmonicon, 002's board falls from 64 damage to 20 and kills nobody. But Panharmonicon converts NOTHING alone — it doubles triggers other cards cause — while the other six above each widen a board on their own text. 007 bounds one board's magnitude, not this stage's availability.

COMBAT. Atarka grants double strike to every attacking Dragon, Thrakkus doubles each Dragon's power, Radiant Destiny is a flat +1/+1, and Scourge of the Throne is the deck's only additional combat phase. Only the first two multiply damage WITHIN a combat; Scourge multiplies the combats instead, a different question the declared leg does not ask.

V2 TOOK TWO CARDS FROM HERE AND NEITHER IS MANA. Dragonback Assault was the landfall widener and a scan of all 95 entries for a trigger on a land entering now returns nothing — five lands arrived in the swap that cut the only card paid for one. Dragonlord Kolaghan was one of two blanket haste grants; Temur Ascendancy and Dragon Tempest's per-entry grant remain, so that half is a copy, not a capability.

In 002 LATHLISS'S OWN ABILITY NEVER FIRES: every entry after her is a token and both nontoken clauses exclude tokens, which keeps the loop finite.

stages.label: WHAT AN ARRIVAL IS WORTH

What the multiplied board produces, priced per entry rather than per turn.

stages.label: THE TURN YOU MUST NOT LOSE
stages.what_it_does:
Eight answers held out of the same open mana for the same turn, and after V2 the stage is exactly the declared component — Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Counterspell, Swan Song, Dovin's Veto, Deflecting Swat — measured 0.781 assembled / 0.673 by turn six at mean turn 2.755, the best-covered part of the deck after ramp. Eerie Interlude left with V2, and it was the deck's only instant-speed exile-blink; what it did about a sweeper is still done four ways here, so what went is a route and not the function.

The finding worth the stage: TWO OF THE EIGHT ARE PROBABLY NOT FREE HERE. Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat both read 'If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost' — you control a permanent, and The Ur-Dragon is a permanent only while it is on the battlefield. The goldfish reports the commander never cast by turn ten in 5,997 of 10,000 iterations and cast by turn six in 5.8% (V1: 7,170 and 4.1% — the mana swap improved this and did not answer it), so for most of most games these are a {2}{W} and a {2}{R} spell rather than free ones. Two limits on that inference, both real: the goldfish counts CASTS, not control — a commander cast on turn seven and killed on turn eight is counted cast while the riders are off — and Hellkite Courser is a second route onto the battlefield that it does not model at all, so 5,997 bounds the answer in neither direction.

V2 also put a ninth answer in another stage. Cavern of Souls makes a Dragon spell paid with its own mana uncounterable, which is a protection clause the 99 did not previously hold; it is filed under mana because a land that taps for mana is mostly a land.

Five of seven sit in a ten-card city that also holds four protection spells and Miirym — three stages in ten cards, and the reason is that the map hears 'a condition on your own stuff' in a cost reducer and in Teferi's Protection alike. The other two are worse addressed: Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug file with the Dragons, because a planeswalker that makes 5/5s and a sorcery that deals 3 to each non-Dragon read as Dragon cards. The clause that puts them in this stage — mana spendable only on Dragon spells — is the quietest line on either card and is scored as zero sources by the deck-builder's own colour maths.

Nine cards, 6/3. Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library', so the map files them in city-3 beside Worldly Tutor and Enlightened Tutor, which cost you a card and are looking for a spell; the three ramp sorceries are looking for a land and cost you none. The same words do two jobs and the map can only see the words — which matters more than usual on this deck, because basics are what logged game 001 turned on. RE-DERIVED THIS ROUND against the 31 land entries' TYPE LINES in cards.json, which is a different source from the one the two previous drafts of this entry used, and it overturns the second of them. TEMPO, and this half stands: Farseek reads 'put it onto the battlefield tapped'; Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim carry no tapped clause, and Skyshroud Claim fetches up to two. So it is those two, not all three, that are the tempo equivalent of city-5's six rocks (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Chromatic Lantern, Dragon's Hoard, Mox Jasper, Relic of Legends), all six of which enter untapped. REACH, and this half is CORRECTED: none of the three says 'basic land card', so each finds any card carrying the named TYPE. Enumerated in full — Farseek's 'Plains, Island, Swamp, or Mountain' reaches 15 entries / 18 copies: the basic Plains, the basic Island, four Mountains, and twelve nonbasics. 'Forest' reaches 9 entries / 11 copies: three basic Forests and EIGHT nonbasics — Breeding Pool, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade, Jetmir's Garden, Overgrown Tomb, Sheltered Thicket, Stomping Ground, Ziatora's Proving Ground. Every one of those eight also carries Mountain, Island, Plains or Swamp, so FARSEEK REACHES ALL EIGHT TOO, and all eight produce green in mana_analysis.lands.list. WITHDRAWN, not amended: 'in a 99 with no Swamp it reaches the basic Plains, the Island and the four Mountains and never a Forest'. It was false eight times over, it undercounted Farseek's nonbasic reach by twelve, and the sentence two clauses above it in that same draft ('each can also find a nonbasic carrying that type') states the rule that refutes it. revision.blind_spots_closed (3) narrates that correction as confirmed and is superseded here on the same point. WHAT SURVIVES, restated to exactly what the enumeration supports: all three can fetch a basic; only two can fetch a BASIC Forest; and the three basic Forests are the only land Nature's Lore or Skyshroud Claim reaches that Farseek cannot. ALSO WITHDRAWN: 'it adds to the 15-of-36 tapped share mana_analysis already flags as over budget'. That 15 counts LANDS and Farseek is a sorcery, so it is not in the share; and all twelve of its nonbasic targets are already inside those 15, the other three tapped lands being Path of Ancestry, Savage Lands and Stormcarved Coast, none of which carries a basic type and none of which Farseek can reach. The tempo cost is real but narrower than that sentence claimed: it lands on the three basics Farseek can find, which would otherwise enter untapped. Seven of its nonbasic targets are shocklands reading 'you may pay 2 life. If you don't, it enters tapped', and whether Farseek's instruction takes that choice away is a rules question rather than a reading of the type line, so it is open_questions[9] and is not assumed either way here.

findings.claim: "ALL THREE can fetch a basic, and only TWO can fetch a Forest. Farseek reads 'a Plains, Island, Swamp, or Mountain card', so in a 99 with no Swamp it reaches the basic Plains, the Island and the four Mountains and never a Forest"
findings.note: This is the widening I was asked to check, and one half of it replaced a false sentence with a different false sentence. Farseek fetches a card with a basic land TYPE, not a basic land, and this 99 holds EIGHT Farseek-legal cards that are also Forests — enumerated from cards.json type lines: Breeding Pool (Forest Island), Canopy Vista (Forest Plains), Cinder Glade (Mountain Forest), Jetmir's Garden (Mountain Forest Plains), Overgrown Tomb (Swamp Forest), Sheltered Thicket (Mountain Forest), Stomping Ground (Mountain Forest), Ziatora's Proving Ground (Swamp Mountain Forest). So 'never a Forest' is wrong eight times over and 'only TWO can fetch a Forest' is wrong once. The enumeration is also short in the other direction: Farseek reaches twelve nonbasics in this deck, not just 'the basic Plains, the Island and the four Mountains'. The paragraph refutes itself two sentences later — 'None of the three says "basic land card", so each can also find a nonbasic carrying that type' — which is exactly why 'never a Forest' cannot stand: in this list the nonbasics carrying Mountain and Swamp are overwhelmingly the ones that also carry Forest. And it is not cosmetic. mana_analysis.json puts green at 17 land sources and 0.831 on-curve from lands alone, which this same stage quotes; every one of those eight is a green source, so the sentence says Farseek cannot reach green when it reaches green eight ways. What IS right, and should survive the fix: 'only TWO can fetch a BASIC Forest' (Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim, against three basic Forests), and 'all three can fetch a basic'. Secondary, in the same entry: 'it adds to the 15-of-36 tapped share mana_analysis already flags as over budget' is loose — the 15 of 36 is a count of LANDS in the 99 and Farseek is a sorcery, so it is not in that share; what it does is make a land arrive tapped that would not otherwise have. The other half of the widening is CORRECT and I checked it card by card: Farseek reads 'put it onto the battlefield tapped', Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim carry no tapped clause, and all six of city-5's members (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Chromatic Lantern, Dragon's Hoard, Mox Jasper, Relic of Legends — read from deck_map.json) enter untapped. Splitting the comparison rather than dropping it was the right call.

The second half of each is wrong about Farseek, eight times over. The orchestrator then WIDENED THE SCOPE DELIBERATELY, on the ground that this is not a claim the swap made stale but one that was always false, and that a reader cannot tell 'out of scope' from 'checked and correct'. THE SAME DECISION WAS THEN MADE A SECOND TIME, on the same entry and the same ground: map_disagreements[5] also called the three ramp sorceries 'functionally the untapped rocks in city-5', which is false of Farseek — it reads 'put it onto the battlefield TAPPED' while Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim carry no tapped clause, and all six of city-5's members enter untapped. Re-derived from the printed cards, not from the sentence. The comparison was SPLIT rather than dropped or hedged, because it survives intact for two of the three and the difference between them is itself the finding. THE SCOPE WAS WIDENED A THIRD TIME, to this note itself, on the ground that superseding by name is not enough: supersession works between documents, not between two fields of one, and a reader landing here would have read the false sentence with no reason to go looking for the entry that overrides it. All three widenings were the orchestrator's call, made explicitly, for the reason that a false claim a reader cannot distinguish from a checked one is worse than an out-of-scope one — and the SECOND of the three was wrong, which is the caution to carry with them rather than the precedent: a scope boundary is cheap to move and expensive to move carelessly, and that is not the same as scope not mattering. Worth carrying into the mechanical check that finding proposes: a validator that refuses an attribution to 'a resolution field that is absent or null in that stack' would have FIRED ON THIS CORRECT CITATION had it resolved `resolution.answers` and stopped there. It must resolve the full path the citation names, and report a path it cannot resolve as unresolved rather than as absent. (2) map_disagreements[5] AND revision.blind_spots_closed (3). The Farseek reach claim was corrected twice and the first correction was itself false ('never a Forest'); the second correction is grounded on the type lines of all 31 land entries in cards.json and is enumerated in the entry. THE COMMON CAUSE OF BOTH, recorded because it is the more useful half: in each case I took a correction from an instruction instead of checking it against the source, in a document whose whole discipline is that a citation is verified against the source. Two of the four corrections ordered on this artifact were wrong in the same way. The rule this leaves behind is DEFER TO THE SOURCE, NOT TO THE ORCHESTRATOR: an instruction that contradicts the artifact is answered by showing the field, not by rewriting the artifact to agree with it.
